2608.03581.title: AI-Assisted Peer Review Across Research Communities: From Reviewer AI Policies to LLM Review Quality
2608.03581.paper_summary: AI-assisted peer review is increasingly discussed and adopted as a tool to support the scientific publishing process, yet there is little systematic understanding of how publication venues regulate its use or of how capable current AI review systems are. We address these questions by first surveying reviewer-facing AI policies across 111 leading AI/NLP conferences and medical journals, revealing substantial regulation differences between the two communities. Second, we evaluate AI-generated peer reviews at ICLR 2026 and Nature Communications using a novel dataset comprising original manuscript submissions and several hundred human- and machine-generated reviews. We compare reviews produced by open-source and proprietary models using complementary evaluation metrics, including LLM-as-a-Judge, score alignment, granularity, and overlap with human reviewers' concerns. Our results show that current LLMs can generate detailed and fluent reviews but exhibit systematic weaknesses, such as overly positive recommendations, generic criticism, and uneven evidence grounding. We demonstrate that aggregate quality scores alone can overestimate review quality and argue for multi-dimensional evaluation of AI-generated peer reviews.
2608.03581.paper_summary_zh: AI輔助的同行評審越來越受到討論並被採用作為支持科學出版過程的工具，然而對於出版場所如何規範其使用或目前的AI評審系統有多大能力，卻缺乏系統性的理解。<lb/>我們通過首先調查111個領先的AI/NLP會議和醫學期刊中的評審者面向的AI政策，來解決這些問題，揭示了這兩個社群之間的實質性規範差異。<lb/>其次，我們使用一個新穎的數據集來評估ICLR 2026和Nature Communications中的AI生成的同行評審，該數據集包含原始手稿提交和數百篇人類和機器生成的評審。<lb/>我們使用互補的評估指標比較開源和專有模型生成的評審，包括LLM作為評審者、分數對齊、細緻度以及與人類評審者關注點的重疊。<lb/>我們的結果顯示，當前的LLM可以生成詳細且流暢的評審，但表現出系統性的弱點，例如過於正面的建議、一般性的批評和不均勻的證據基礎。<lb/>我們證明僅依賴總體質量分數可能會高估評審質量，並主張對AI生成的同行評審進行多維度的評估。
